Panthers vs Tigers Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 27 2026
September 5 th 2026, 5:06pm , By: Ben Bridge
The final Sunday afternoon game of the regular season is one of the strangest betting propositions of Round 27 because we will know considerably more by kick-off than we do when betting early in the week.
Penrith and the Warriors enter Round 27 locked on 40 competition points, with New Zealand holding a differential advantage of just +309 to +308. The Warriors play Manly on Saturday afternoon, meaning Ivan Cleary’s side will know exactly what is required to claim the minor premiership before taking the field at CommBank Stadium.
That makes Wests Tigers +19.5 the early play. If Manly upset the Warriors, Penrith need only win. If the Warriors scrape home by a small margin, the Panthers may still need some points differential, but nowhere near the type of enormous score the current spread implies.
There is also the finals management factor. Isaah Yeo remains among the reserves as he nears a return from a pectoral injury, while Mitch Kenny returns from a long injury lay off. Izack Tago is out with a knee injury and Luke Garner shifts into the centres.
Wests have also shown considerably more fight over the past fortnight than they did through their horrific mid-season slump.
Panthers vs Tigers Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 27
Panthers Professional Rather Than Spectacular
Penrith’s 24-10 win over Canterbury last Friday was exactly the sort of performance you would expect from a team preparing for September. They were not spectacular. They did not need to be.
The Panthers completed an extraordinary 38 of 41 sets, controlled field position and simply kept the Bulldogs at arm’s length for the entire evening. That is important when assessing a 19.5-point handicap.
Penrith are capable of producing enormous attacking numbers, nobody needs reminding after the 68-0 result against these Tigers earlier in the year, but Ivan Cleary’s focus now is preparation for the finals rather than entertaining the crowd.
Nathan Cleary remains the best game manager in the competition and can dictate exactly how much risk Penrith need to take once the Saturday result is known.
Dylan Edwards is back at fullback, Brian To’o remains on the wing and Mitch Kenny’s return gives the spine greater stability. Jack Cole continues at five-eighth.
The forward pack is still strong even with Yeo uncertain. Moses Leota, Liam Henry, Isaiah Papali’i, Liam Martin and Lindsay Smith provide more than enough quality to control the Tigers through the middle.
Yeo being listed among the reserves adds another late mail variable. If he returns, Penrith become stronger, but his minutes could easily be managed before finals.
The same logic applies across the team. If Penrith are 20 points ahead after an hour and the minor premiership is secured, there is no reason to keep key players unnecessarily exposed.
That is exactly why laying -19.5 early in the week is dangerous.
Tigers Show Some Backbone in Townsville
Wests’ 24-10 loss to North Queensland ended the brief high created by their stunning Roosters upset, but the performance was far from the type of capitulation we saw earlier in the season.
The Tigers remained competitive for most of the night and were still threatening to make things interesting late, with Terrell May having a try disallowed for obstruction in the 65th minute. North Queensland did not finally secure the result until Tom Chester scored with three minutes remaining.
That followed the extraordinary 25-24 victory over the Roosters. Two games do not repair a dreadful season, but they do suggest Benji Marshall has managed to get some late fight back into the group.
Jarome Luai and Jock Madden remain in the halves, with Jahream Bula at fullback and Api Koroisau controlling the ruck. Terrell May and Fonua Pole give Wests enough size through the middle to ensure Penrith cannot simply coast through contact.

The final two games of the regular season hold plenty of interest with the minor premiership to be decided in the last game of the round.
Sunday's opening game however saw the Eels out to continue their late resurgence/
In the lead-up, the Eels had knocked off Wests Tigers, Cowboys and Sharks across the past five rounds and almost pulled off the biggest comeback in NRL history against Souths.
They headed to Wollongong to confront a Dragons team desperate to finish a horror season on a positive note before a host of key signings come on board in 2027.
In an entertaining and seesawing match, the home side prevailed, with departing Dragons Blake Lawrie and Tyrell Sloan amongst the try scorers - with Sloan slotting the winning two-point field goal to boot in the 24-22 win.
The final regular season fixture pits the Panthers against Wests Tigers, another team keen to put 2026 in the rearview mirror after being unable to carry the momentum of a 5-2 start to the season.
A win by two points by the Panthers would see them clinch the minor premiership.

items.title: Joey: Jett Cleary’s Panthers deal spells trouble for out-of-favour star - nine.com.au
items.snippet: Joey: Jett Cleary’s Panthers deal spells trouble for out-of-favour star    nine.com.au
items.body_excerpt:
Rugby league Immortal Andrew Johns has questioned if out-of-favour Panthers playmaker Blaize Talagi has a future at the foot of the mountains, in light of Jett Cleary’s stellar NRL debut and Penrith’s other halves.
The Panthers must beat Wests Tigers by more than two points at CommBank Stadium on Sunday if they are to claim the minor premiership, after the Warriors edged the Sea Eagles 31-30 in an Auckland thriller on Saturday.
Nathan Cleary (left) and Blaize Talagi. NRL Imagery.
Intriguingly, Panthers coach Ivan Cleary has again opted against using Talagi as the halves partner of his champion son Nathan , instead going for Jack Cole.
Cogger, who is unavailable for the final-round match because of a suspension, has been preferred over Talagi at five-eighth in other weeks.
And Talagi’s mission to win back the No.6 jumper will become even harder when Jett Cleary crosses from the Warriors to the Panthers in the off-season, although Cole is off to the Bears.
Penrith went all chips in on Talagi after the exit of Jarome Luai following the 2024 season, and the 21-year-old is contracted to the Panthers until the end of 2027, but his future at the premiership powerhouse is murky.
“Moving forward, I don’t know if he’s got a future there at Penrith,” Johns said on Wide World of Sports’ Immortal Behaviour .
Read more
Turbo blunder duds Manly as field goal snatches victory for Warriors
“Jett Cleary’s coming back, then you’ve got Jack Cole and Jack Cogger. So he’s gone down the pecking order. Interesting to see.
“Big off-season for Blaize.”
Jett Cleary, who like Talagi is 21, had a magnificent NRL debut against the Knights in Auckland last week.
Lining up at halfback, the former Panthers junior set up three tries and kicked brilliantly to steer the Warriors to a 46-32 win.
His famous dad and brother, Ivan and Nathan, watched from the stands as he made his mark on the NRL stage.
There’s no doubting Talagi’s attacking spark, but Johns cast doubt over his defence.
Jett Cleary and his family after his brilliant NRL debut. Hannah Peters/Getty Images
“Blaize early in the year, when Canterbury put a score on them [the Panthers], Jacob Preston terrorised them – terrorised Blaize and also Casey McLean, with that gap between them,” the legendary halfback said.
“And I’ve sort of felt since then his confidence has been knocked around, but also he’s been targeted defensively. And if you show any weaknesses, teams just sit on it, so it’s an area of his game he’s got to improve, Blaize.
“Ivan’s got a mentality of defence. Jack Cole’s a really good defender, Jack Cogger will come back in.
“... They put him on late against the Chooks and he looked a bit all at sea, threw an intercept, and his confidence is down.”
As for Jett Cleary?
“He’s good,” Johns said.
“He’s a tough boy.”
